title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: A historically charged Wesleyan concert captured on a low‑fidelity audience mic – the tape is muddy and often inaudible, but the protest‑era atmosphere makes it memorable.
ai_review.review: The recording is an amateur crowd‑mic capture with frequent drop‑outs, a falling microphone and a home‑brew mix that leaves the band barely audible.  Despite the technical shortcomings, the show is remembered for its anti‑war vibe, an acoustic opener (now missing), a New Riders set featuring Jerry’s pedal steel, and a few dead‑head moments like Pigpen on keys.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the tape very poorly because of its terrible audio quality; only a handful praise the historical context, yielding an overall low but not disastrous score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crowd microphone frequently falls over, home‑brew mix, band barely heard; lots of talking, laughter and ambient noise; occasional moments of clearer music but overall muddy and unlistenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set (missing from tape) → New Riders of the Purple Sage set with Jerry’s pedal steel → Grateful Dead main set.  The concert was intertwined with anti‑war protests and a relaxed, communal atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel highlighted during the NRPS portion; acoustic set mentioned but not present on tape.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s keyboards praised as a high point of the evening.
